texts.li: There's a {X_kind} on the colony's land who has never lived under a roof, and keeps to the edges where the colony's people can see. {A_nameDef} has watched {X_objective} take food left out and says {X_pronoun} could be brought in, slowly, the way an animal is. {B_nameDef} doesn't like being watched, and would see {X_objective} sent on.

[lowtech] The {X_kind} has been seen again at the edge of the trees, the one who lives like the deer do. The old people say such a one can be gentled with food and patience, though some bite the hand. {A_nameDef} would try. {B_nameDef} says leave {X_objective} to the wild, or chase {X_objective} off.

[!lowtech] A {X_kind}, no faction and no words anyone has heard, has been living off the colony's edges for days. {A_nameDef}, the colony's best with animals, thinks {X_pronoun} could be tamed like one. {B_nameDef} wants {X_objective} off the land.
[land:forest] Someone has been sleeping under the trees past the colony and slipping away at dawn: a {X_kind}, {A_nameDef} says, watching the colony as warily as the colony watches {X_objective}.

li.label: {A_nameDef} tries to bring {X_objective} in
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is marked for taming, and {A_nameDef} and the other handlers will try with food and patience.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {A_nameDef} sets out food at the edge of the trees, a little closer each day, the old way.

li.label: Let {X_objective} be
li.outcome: The colony leaves {X_nameDef} to the edges of its land. {X_pronoun} watches, and the colony watches back.

li.label: Drive {X_objective} off the land
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} takes fright at last and goes off the colony's land at a run.

texts.li: The storm took down a stretch of the pen's {THING}, and {A_nameDef} found the gap at first light with the {BEAST} already nosing at it. {B_nameDef} can put it back today. {A_nameDef} says let them out a while: there's grazing past the pen, and the crops are close too.

[big] {COUNT} animals in the pen, and a gap in its {THING} where the storm leaned on it. {B_nameDef} wants it mended before they find it. {A_nameDef} says a few days on the open grass would do the {BEAST} good, if they keep out of the fields.

[lowtech] The wind in the night brought down part of the pen's {THING}. The {BEAST} have found the gap and stand looking out of it. {B_nameDef} has the tools ready to mend it; {A_nameDef} would let them graze outside for a while.
[!lowtech] Storm damage: a section of the pen's {THING} is down, and the {BEAST} can walk out through it. {B_nameDef} can rebuild it. {A_nameDef} points out the grass beyond is better than the pen's.

li.label: Mend it today
li.outcome: The gap is marked for {B_nameDef} and the builders to put back, and the handlers will bring the {BEAST} in once it's closed.

li.label: Let them graze outside a while
li.outcome: The gap is left open, and the {BEAST} graze where they like until the colony mends it.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] The gap is left open, the old way, and the {BEAST} wander out to the better grass.

texts.li: The wild ambrosia {PLACE} is ripe, {COUNT} bushes heavy with it, and {A_nameDef} came back with sticky hands. It's worth a great deal, and it's a joy to eat. {B_nameDef} says it pulls at some people who eat it, and would leave it on the bush.

[teetotal] {COUNT} ambrosia bushes are ripe {PLACE}. {A_nameDef} wants them picked for the stores. {B_nameDef} has never touched anything of the kind, and says the colony would be better off if nobody did.

[lowtech] The sweet fruit the elders call a gift is ripe on {COUNT} bushes {PLACE}. {A_nameDef} would pick it all. {B_nameDef} says some who eat it want nothing else after, and that a little, for one night, is enough.

[!lowtech] The ambrosia {PLACE} is ripe: {COUNT} bushes, worth good silver, and sweet enough that some eaters come back for more than they should. {A_nameDef} wants it in the stores. {B_nameDef} would pick only enough for one night.

li.label: Pick it all for the stores
li.outcome: Every ripe ambrosia bush is marked for the pickers, and the fruit goes to the stores.

li.label: Enough for one night
li.outcome: As many bushes as the colony has people are marked for the pickers. The rest stay on the bush.

li.label: Leave it on the bush
li.outcome: The ambrosia is left where it grows. {A_nameDef} goes past it every day and looks.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} nearly stepped on them: {COUNT} eggs in a scrape in the grass {PLACE}, still warm, and no {BEAST} anywhere near. {B_nameDef} says kept warm they'll hatch, and the young would be the colony's to raise. {A_nameDef} says eggs are eggs, and the cooks would thank them.

[lowtech] A {BEAST}'s nest with {COUNT} eggs in it, {PLACE}, and the mother gone. The old way is to take one and leave the rest. {B_nameDef} would take them all and hatch them by the fire; {A_nameDef} would take them for the pot.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} found a clutch of {COUNT} {BEAST} eggs {PLACE}, abandoned and still warm. {B_nameDef} says they'd hatch in the warm stores. {A_nameDef} says the kitchen would make better use of them.
[land:grassland] Out in the long grass {PLACE}, {A_nameDef} found {COUNT} {BEAST} eggs in a hollow, the nest left. {B_nameDef} wants to see what hatches; {A_nameDef} wants an omelette.

li.label: Keep them warm and raise what hatches
li.outcome: The eggs are carried in to the warm, and whatever hatches is the colony's to raise.

li.label: For the kitchen
li.outcome: The eggs go to the stores for the cooks, and none of them will hatch.

li.label: Leave them where they lie
li.outcome: The eggs are left in the grass. If anything hatches, it hatches wild.
